grading_policy: Every requested material part separately; equivalent wording accepted, unasked extra details not demanded, no borrowing facts between answers. Confidence labels ignored.
benchmark_validity: SUPERSEDED: later essential defense-source gap recorded. Historical fixed-key recovery counts do not establish a complete core PASS.

grades.question: During attrition, how does an office roll resolve, what extra modifier does the Chairman have, and where do a retiring member, card and fatigue go?
grades.expected_answer: Roll separately per office card, +1 per fatigue and an additional +1 for Chairman. 1–2 nothing, 3–4 add fatigue, 5+ retire: member to Pensioners, card flipped into Vacant Offices, fatigue returned to supply.
grades.observed_answer: During London Season, roll one die simultaneously for each office card a player holds. Add one to that office’s roll for each fatigue on its card; the Chairman also adds one. A modified 1–2 does nothing, 3–4 adds fatigue to the card, and 5 or higher retires the officeholder. Move the retiring member to Pensioners, flip the office card into Vacant Offices, and return that card’s fatigue to the supply. Commanders have no office card and do not make these normal attrition rolls.
grades.reason: Attrition thresholds, per-fatigue and Chairman modifiers, and pensioner/card/fatigue destinations are all explicit.

grades.question: Who may select London Season cards, in what order and with which tiebreakers? What happens to the display and unused pensioners afterward?
grades.expected_answer: Each player retiring at least one pensioner must take or discard one display card, descending actual total retirement spending; ties most total windows then PM clockwise order. May peek at display blackmails. Stop when display empty. Discard remaining display and refill three, blackmail down/prestige up even if none taken. Return unretired pensioners to supply.
grades.observed_answer: Only players who retired at least one pensioner may take or discard a London Season display card. They act in descending order of their actual total retirement spending. Ties go first to the player with the most total windows, counting newly acquired prizes, then clockwise from the Prime Minister. The acting player may peek at display blackmails. Do not replace cards as players select or discard; if the display empties, skip every remaining eligible player immediately. After selection, discard all remaining display cards and refill to exactly three cards: prestige faceup and blackmail facedown, even if nobody selected a card. Return all unused pensioners to their supplies.
summary_evidence: I. London Season — Retirements and Prestige
grades.reason: Eligibility, actual spending order, both tiebreakers, take/discard, no immediate replacement, empty-display skip, faceup/down refill and pensioner return are resolved.

grades.question: How do the opportunity marker and extra-action laws affect family actions? If four offices are vacant and the marker already sits on Enlist Writer, how many writers can be placed?
grades.expected_answer: Normal selected action once, or twice if marker already there at phase start; move marker to main action. Only latest passed extra-action law usable, extra action gets no marker doubling and does not move marker. Four or more vacancies allow one extra writer once per turn, so repeated Enlist Writer can place three total.
grades.observed_answer: At the start of the Family phase, each player checks which action their opportunity marker matched at phase start. They choose a main action once, or may take it twice if the marker already matched that action, then move the marker onto the chosen main action. Afterward, only the latest passed extra-action law may grant an extra action; that action is never doubled by the marker and does not move it. With four vacant offices and the marker already on Enlist Writer, the player may take Enlist Writer twice, and the four-vacancy bonus adds one writer once that turn, for three writers total.
summary_evidence: II. Family — action sequence and Enlist Writer
grades.reason: Ordinary main action, phase-start matching/doubling, marker movement, latest extra law without marker effects and three-writer once-per-turn bonus are resolved.

grades.question: After Seek Share actions, how are new Company shares created and remaining applicants moved? Where was the initial purchase money paid?
grades.expected_answer: Seek Share pays printed empty Stock Exchange space price to bank. At end Family, while Debt and applicants remain, move rightmost applicant into Court and reduce Debt one per share. With no Debt, shift remaining applicants as far right as possible preserving order. Money does not enter Company treasury.
grades.observed_answer: After all Family actions, while both Debt and Stock Exchange applicants remain, move the rightmost applicant into Court and reduce Debt by one; repeat while both remain. Court pieces are Company shares. Once Debt is zero, slide any remaining applicants as far right as possible while preserving their order. The purchase money for Seek Share was paid to the bank at the queue space’s printed cost; it never went into Company treasuries.
summary_evidence: II. Family — Seek Share; New Company shares
grades.reason: Rightmost-first issue while Debt exists, one Debt reduction per share, order-preserving shift and bank payment destination are all supplied.

grades.question: When hiring, how are vacancies ordered, what consent does hiring your own family require, what happens to promoted fatigue, and what if no candidate or hirer exists?
grades.expected_answer: Ascending back-of-card office numbers, insert promotion vacancy in ascending order; own-family hiring needs verbal consent of every other player represented in candidate pool, except Chairman election. Promoted fatigue travels to new card. No candidate or vacant hiring office means skip office; remains vacant and takes no actions including hiring.
grades.observed_answer: Fill vacant offices in ascending order by the number on each office card’s back. The designated hirer chooses a candidate, who moves into the office, and that candidate’s family gets the office card. For an ordinary office hire into your own family, obtain verbal consent from every other player represented in that office’s candidate pool. Chairman elections and Commander appointments are exempt from this Nepotism consent rule. When promoting an officeholder, transfer that office’s fatigue to the new card and insert the old card, now vacant, into the ascending hiring order. If there is no eligible candidate or the hirer is vacant, skip the office; it remains vacant and takes no actions, including hiring.
grades.reason: Ascending vacancies, promotion insertion/fatigue, all represented-family consent with Chairman/Commander exceptions, and absent-candidate/hirer skipping are explicit.

grades.question: How is a Chairman elected, how does a deadlocked election resolve, and does the elected Chairman piece remain a tradable Company share?
grades.expected_answer: Candidate must own share, needs consent of players controlling pure majority (>half) current shares; first to achieve support elected. Deadlock former Chairman picks any shareholder including self without Nepotism. Winner moves one share into Chairman slot; still share but cannot trade it or use it for firm investment.
grades.observed_answer: The former Chairman first announces how many shares are required for a pure majority, meaning more than half of the current shares. Any shareholder may campaign; the first candidate supported by players controlling that number of shares wins. Move one of the winner’s Company shares into the Chairman slot and give them the title marker. If no candidate gets the required support, the former Chairman chooses any shareholder, including themself, without Nepotism consent. The Chairman piece still counts as a share for dividends, majority calculations and scoring, but cannot be traded or invested in a firm. If the Court is empty, the former Chairman automatically returns as Chairman, placing a family member from supply or, if necessary and possible, taking one from a prize and losing that prize’s VP; if this is impossible, there is no Chairman.
grades.reason: Pure-majority shareholder election, deadlock former-Chairman choice including self without Nepotism, and continuing untradable/noninvestable share status are supplied.

grades.question: Explain success-check results, payment, retries, catastrophic destinations and the restriction against dead actions.
grades.expected_answer: Commit office treasury money/resources, gather dice then subtract penalty; lowest die 1–2 success, 3–4 failure retry if sufficient resources, 5–6 catastrophe: no more office actions, officeholder to supply, card flipped to Vacant Offices, fatigue to supply (specific office exceptions apply). No action without effect or chance of success.
grades.observed_answer: For a Company-office success check, first commit the resources and cash; all cash for the check comes from that acting office’s treasury and is paid to the bank. Gather dice, subtract penalties, and roll. Use the lowest die: 1–2 succeeds; 3–4 fails and may be retried if resources and office-specific limits allow; 5–6 is catastrophic, ends that office’s actions, returns its officeholder to supply, discards its fatigue and flips its card into Vacant Offices. Specific Commander and firm procedures can modify this. Do not take a dead action that has no effect or chance of success, such as trading with no ship or deploying without dice to trigger possible officer losses.
grades.reason: Acting-office cash paid to bank, resources minus penalty, lowest-die results/retries, catastrophic destinations and no-dead-action rule are explicit.

grades.question: What are the Chairman’s voluntary borrowing and allocation duties, including consent and track limits?
grades.expected_answer: May advance Debt three times freely, +£5 Balance each. Each further advancement needs majority-shareholder consent including Chairman share; cannot pass Debt track end. Must allocate all Company Balance to other office treasuries, reducing Balance accordingly; borrowing may interleave allocation while respecting limit.
grades.observed_answer: The Chairman may add up to three Debt without consent, receiving £5 Balance for each advance. Each additional advance requires consent from players controlling a majority of Company shares, counting the Chairman, and Debt may never pass the end of its track. The Chairman must allocate all Balance to other offices’ treasuries, reducing Balance by the amount transferred. Borrowing and allocation may be interleaved as long as the total borrowing follows these limits; money already in office treasuries stays there for those offices to use.
grades.reason: Three free £5 advances, further majority consent including Chairman, track limit, all-Balance allocation and allowed interleaving are resolved.

grades.question: What must Shipping do with its budget? State ship costs, destinations, consent requirements and the prerequisite for buying Company ships.
grades.expected_answer: Spend until at most £2 remains. Lease extra £2, fit shipyard ship £3 without owner consent, buy Company £5 only with no ships remaining on shipyards. Place acquired ships in any sea zone (China eligible once created). Extras return at Refresh.
grades.observed_answer: The Manager of Shipping must spend its treasury until £2 or less remains. It may lease an extra ship for £2, fit a ship from a shipyard for £3 without the owner’s consent, or buy a Company ship for £5 only if no ships remain on shipyards. Put each acquired ship in any sea zone, including China once that office exists. Leased extra ships remain only until Refresh.
grades.reason: Mandatory spending endpoint, all three costs, shipyard consent waiver, Company-ship prerequisite and sea-zone destinations are supplied.

grades.question: For a President’s Trade action, explain declared regions, dice penalty, routes and capacity, insufficient writers, protected home regions, bonuses and successful-trade limit.
grades.expected_answer: Declare home plus only actually reachable regions with sufficient ships and open route; £1 per die minus one per nonhome declared region. Success fill as many orders as possible in declared regions, one per ship, first home port then adjacent own placed writers. Use filled tokens if writers exhausted. Cannot fill another Presidency home region even vacant. Company receives printed order values, President £1 per filled order, writer owner £1 per writer placed; at most one successful trade per President per turn. Revenue exception: under Deregulation an order already filled by a firm this turn pays the Company half listed value, rounded down; President and writer bonuses remain unchanged.
grades.observed_answer: The President chooses when its own Trade occurs relative to its Commander and Governors, but must give each position an opportunity; a position may decline, and one position must finish before the next begins. If the President is vacant, the Chairman sets the order but cannot trade or approve local-alliance purchases. For Trade, declare the home region and only regions reachable from it through open orders with available ship capacity. Each £1 from the Presidency treasury buys one die, and subtract one die per declared nonhome region. A failed attempt may be retried if affordable; retries belong to that President’s uninterrupted opportunity, so another position cannot act between them. A President can have at most one successful Trade per turn. On success, fill one order per ship in its sea zone, as many as possible within declared regions: the first writer goes to the home port, and each next order must be adjacent to one already filled by that Presidency. Use actual writers while available, then filled-order tokens. A President cannot fill another President’s home region even if that office is vacant. Add each order’s printed value to Balance, or half rounded down if a firm already filled it this turn; the President gets £1 from the bank per order and each writer owner gets £1 per writer placed.
grades.source_references: Rules pp20–21; lines 1540–1582; Rules p40 lines2817–2820; p41 example
grades.reason: Home/reachable declarations, dice penalties, connected home-first capacity and token substitution, protected home regions, personal bonuses and one successful Trade are explicit; half-value firm-refill exception is included.

grades.question: What can a Commander target with Deploy, what produces dice and penalties, and when and how are officer losses checked?
grades.expected_answer: Target home, associated region or bordering associated region; exclude another home or another Presidency Company region. Own Company target requires closed order/unrest. Exhaust active officers/regiments for one die each, alliances for printed strength, subtract the combined strength of target and all OTHER regions in its empire (target counted once); Company-controlled defending strength zero. After every attempt roll per exhausted officer, each 6 removes an officer to its owner supply, never regiment.
grades.observed_answer: A Commander may Deploy against a region in its own Presidency’s home, any region associated with that Presidency, or any region bordering an associated region. It cannot target another Presidency’s home or a Company-controlled region belonging to another Presidency. A Company region must have unrest or a closed order for the action to have an effect. Exhaust selected officers and regiments for one die each and local alliances for their printed dice; subtract the strength of the target and all other regions in its empire, counting the target only once. Company-controlled defense strength is zero. After every attempt, each owner rolls one die per officer exhausted in that attempt; each 6 returns that officer to supply. Regiments do not roll for officer losses. A noncatastrophic failure may be retried with remaining resources.
grades.source_references: Rules p22; lines 1617–1650; Rules p22 lines1639–1645; p7 lines707–711
grades.reason: All target permissions/exclusions, own-Company effect requirement, resource dice, target-counted-once empire penalty and zero Company strength, and per-attempt officer-six losses are given.

grades.question: On successful Deploy how are loot and trophies calculated and control imposed? What changes if Deploy catastrophically fails?
grades.expected_answer: Loot £4 per tower plus faceup loot modifier, at least surviving used officers+1. Pay Commander £1 plus £1 per own used surviving officer, clockwise other officers, then £1 bank per regiment/alliance piece; repeat until empty. Commander trophy per tower; remove tower/dome, capital matching flags, clear unrest/open all orders. Newly conquer: loot token region-side above President, Governor overlay placed in conquered region and ONLY office card to Vacant Offices stack, Company control; inward redirect Elephant if formerly poised outward there. Catastrophe loses half trophies rounded up and Commander to supply; still check exhausted officer losses.
grades.observed_answer: On a successful Deploy, loot taken from the bank is £4 per target tower plus the faceup loot modifier, with a minimum equal to the surviving officers used in that attempt plus one. Count only surviving participating officers and the regiments and alliances used in that attempt. Distribute each payout cycle in this order: £1 for the Commander plus £1 for each of their used surviving officers; then £1 per used surviving officer of each other family clockwise; then £1 per used regiment and per used local-alliance piece to the bank. Repeat the whole cycle from the Commander until the loot is spent. The Commander also gets one trophy per target tower. Then remove the target tower and dome; if it was an empire capital, remove all matching empire flags; open all its orders and remove all its unrest. If it was not already Company-controlled, put its loot/control token region-side up above the associated President’s box, put the Governor overlay on the conquered region, and send only the Governor office card to Vacant Offices for later hiring. Do not create Governors/overlays if a Governor General is in play. If the Elephant was in the conquered region facing outward, move it fully inside. On catastrophic failure, the Commander returns half their family’s trophies rounded up and returns to supply; exhausted officers still roll for losses, and there is no successful-control procedure.
summary_evidence: Actions — Commanders and Deploy; Successful control procedure
grades.reason: Loot formula/minimum, clockwise repeating payout and bank pieces, trophies, capital/Elephant cleanup, new Governorship destinations and catastrophic trophy/member/loss effects are resolved.

grades.question: How does Governor Administer work across repeated attempts, including bonuses, tax unrest and stopping?
grades.expected_answer: Start printed dice pool; roll pool, no penalty, lose one die after any attempt. Success £1 bonus, extra £1 if preceding roll failed, choose build Company ship in two successful stages, regiment in associated army, or unsplit £2 Balance/President treasury. Tax after first in turn adds unrest. Any unsuccessful check adds unrest. May repeat until stop, pool exhausted or catastrophe (general vacancy rule).
grades.observed_answer: A Governor takes the printed dice pool and may make repeated Administer attempts. Each attempt rolls the current pool without a penalty, then reduces the pool by one regardless of result. On success, take £1, or £2 if the immediately preceding roll was unsuccessful, and choose exactly one benefit: Build a Company ship, Commission a regiment, or Tax. A ship requires two successful Build actions: if there is no partially built ship in the region, place one there; otherwise complete it into the sea zone associated with the Governor’s President. A commissioned regiment goes into that President’s Army, has officer-like strength, pays loot to the bank, and causes no officer-loss rolls. Tax adds an unsplit £2 to Company Balance or that President’s treasury; each Tax after the first that turn adds unrest in the region. Any unsuccessful roll adds one unrest there; catastrophe also removes the officeholder under the normal rule. Continue with the shrinking pool until the Governor stops, no dice remain, or catastrophe occurs.
grades.reason: Diminishing pool and result-independent decrement, immediate-previous-failure bonus, two separate Build stages/destinations, associated Army, unsplit Tax/unrest and stop conditions are resolved.

grades.question: If Company revenue cannot cover expenses, how do emergency loans work at and below max Debt, how does Standing change, and when are expectations and dividends checked?
grades.expected_answer: Expenses £1 per current Debt, officer/regiment excluding Commander, ship in sea zones including China. Emergency loans +£5 each, advance Debt if possible even at maximum continue borrowing; added Debt costs no current-turn interest, then Balance zero. 1–2 emergency loans Standing -1; 3+ -2. Then compare Balance with expectations at current Standing, if below Standing -1. Then optional dividends £1 per share incl Chairman; total dividend payout strictly greater than expectations advances Standing once. Immediate failure when Standing reaches failure.
grades.observed_answer: During Company expenses, reduce Balance by £1 for each existing Debt, each officer or regiment in an Army, and each ship in a sea zone including China; exclude Commanders. If Balance cannot cover expenses, take £5 emergency loans, advancing Debt one step per loan until the Debt track ends. Continue receiving loans even at maximum Debt. Emergency Debt creates no additional expense this turn. After taking emergency loans, set Balance to zero. One or two loans lower Standing one space; three or more lower it two spaces. Then compare the remaining Balance to the expectations for current Standing; if it is below expectations, lower Standing one. After that, the Chairman may pay any affordable number of dividends, each costing one cash per Company share and paying each share owner £1 per share, including the Chairman. If total dividend cash paid is strictly greater than expectations, advance Standing one space.
summary_evidence: VI. Revenue — Company expenses, expectations, dividends
grades.reason: Loan amount/track-cap/no-current-turn-interest, zero Balance, Standing loan bands, current expectations next, optional dividends and strict enthusiasm inequality are supplied; unasked expense/dividend formulas are not required.

grades.question: When Company regions face a Crisis, which regions are attacked, in what order and at what strength? How is defense mounted and what happens on successful defense?
grades.expected_answer: Resolve primary first then all other Company regions with unrest, Bombay/Madras/Bengal Army order; each Commander orders own regions. Primary normal invasion/rebellion strength + local unrest, secondary unrest only. Exhaust newly active Army strength equal attack or as much as possible; insufficient means Region Loss. Successful defense clears unrest and Commander gains trophy. Vacant Commander replaced by Military Affairs then Chairman, acting substitute gains/loses no trophies. Additionally, if the primary Crisis was a normal Invasion which failed against the Company, remove one tower level from the attacker if possible.
grades.observed_answer: A Crisis is resolved at the Elephant’s location, with its tail as attacker and head as target, then the Elephant marches. For an Invasion Crisis, compare the sovereign attacker’s whole empire strength plus event modifier against the defender’s whole empire strength; success requires strictly greater strength. On failure, the attacker loses one tower. For a Rebellion Crisis, compare only the rebelling region’s strength plus modifier against its sovereign capital’s strength; other empire regions do not count, and success also requires strictly greater strength. On failure, remove one tower from the capital. For an attack on a Company region, resolve secondary Rebellions in every other Company region with unrest after the primary attack; their order is primary first, then Bombay, Madras, Bengal, with each Commander ordering attacks within their Presidency. A normal primary Invasion/Rebellion attack strength is its ordinary strength plus unrest in the target. A primary Foreign Invasion uses only its ordinary attack die, without added unrest. A secondary Rebellion’s strength is only the number of unrest cubes in that secondary region, without event modifier or empire strength. The associated Commander must exhaust active Army pieces totaling that attack strength or as much as possible, using local alliances at printed strength and not splitting them. If newly exhausted defense is insufficient, apply Region Loss. If sufficient, remove all unrest in that attacked region and give the Commander one trophy; if this successful defense defeated a normal primary Invasion, also remove one tower from the attacking region if possible. If the primary Invasion succeeds against the Company, apply empire growth. When the Commander position is vacant, Military Affairs acts in its stead, or the Chairman if Military Affairs is vacant; that player chooses defense pieces and gains or loses no trophies.
summary_evidence: VII. Events in India — Crisis; Attacks on Company; Region Loss
grades.source_references: Rules p33; lines 2262–2296; Rules p33 lines2290–2296
grades.reason: Historical frozen key: primary-first and Presidency/Commander order, unrest-only secondaries, primary strength, compulsory defense and vacant substitutes, trophy/unrest cleanup and failed-primary-Invasion attacker tower loss are supplied. Subsequent source-gap discovery invalidates any complete core signoff for excess alliance strength.
grades.source_completeness_warning: Historical key did not settle an indivisible alliance exceeding attack strength. Correct means recovery of the historical asked/known procedure only; no definitive overshoot ruling or complete core PASS.

grades.question: What happens when a law fails versus passes, including support-zero, policy movement, Prime Minister and effect order?
grades.expected_answer: Support -1 or lower fails; discard and resolve dilemma If Failed, Opposition Leader returns marker and becomes PM, moves selected policy one adjacent space either way and resolves it. Zero or higher passes: law with passed laws, PM gains token, selected policy consequence then immediate law effects. Restore vote cards. If legislation fails Company, finish vote then final scoring.
grades.observed_answer: The Prime Minister reveals up to three laws one at a time, chooses one, and discards the others; drawing a dilemma forces selection and ends drawing. The PM chooses direction around the dial and stops on the first policy space matching the law’s bottom icon, chooses its target and consequence, reads the law, and sets Vote to its printed starting support. Voting starts with the PM and proceeds clockwise; each £1 of family cash buys one vote, plus printed card votes, with used cards rotated. Players may adjust support up or down. The PM may call another full round or stop after each; a round with no votes ends voting. A player may switch from supporting to opposing during this vote, but after opposing cannot support it. Track opposition votes; the biggest opponent holds Opposition Leader, with the current holder retaining it on a tie. With the recipient’s consent, votes may be cast for someone who already opposed or commits to oppose and count toward their opposition total. The PM cannot oppose or consent to enterprises opposing, except when forced by the “Vote with my enterprises” promise. At support −1 or less, the law fails: discard it, resolve a dilemma’s If Failed text, the Opposition Leader returns the token and takes the PM dial, and the new PM moves the proposed policy one space in either direction and resolves that adjacent policy. At support zero or higher, it passes: place it among passed laws, give the PM a passed-law token, resolve the selected policy first and then the law’s immediate effects. Restore every used voting card to its regular orientation after either outcome. If a law causes Company failure, finish the vote before Final Scoring.
summary_evidence: VIII. Parliament Meets — Voting and Resolution
grades.reason: Negative failure versus zero-or-positive passage, law/dilemma handling, PM transfer/adjacent policy, policy-before-immediate-law order, vote-card restoration and finish-vote failure timing are supplied.

grades.question: When can or must a Deregulation session be called in the relevant scenarios, and what are its success/failure effects and exceptions from ordinary voting?
grades.expected_answer: 1758/Long1710 start-turn before London: PM may if Standing and/or Debt lined, must if either starred. Pass reduce Debt one per two Debt, Standing to S, PM law token, activate deregulation. Failure raise share VP value up to ±3, law kept, PM stays. No policy and PM may vote against.
grades.observed_answer: In 1758 and Long 1710, at the start of a turn before London Season, the PM may call a special Deregulation vote if Standing and/or Debt is on a lined space, and must call it if either is on a starred space. The ordinary voting procedure and support threshold apply, with these exceptions: Deregulation has no policy, the PM may vote against it, and failure neither removes the PM nor discards the Deregulation law. If it passes, lower Debt by one for every two current Debt, set Standing to S, give the PM a passed-law token, and activate firms. If it fails, increase Company share scoring value by flipping or placing the Court VP token, up to a maximum of ±3. The 1813 scenario begins deregulated.
grades.reason: Correct scenarios/before-London timing, lined/starred triggers, both outcomes, share-value cap and all special voting exceptions are resolved.

grades.question: How can a firm be formed or invested in, where does money come from, and what restrictions apply to Company shares, invested workshops and the ten-share limit?
grades.expected_answer: Nonmanager forms by returning eligible Company share or flipping workshop invested; flip own board, create family firm share, value leftmost, £5 bank to London. Later investment manager consent, same share/workshop payment gives £5 London and new share. Weak Company share when Standing/Debt lined prohibited; same-turn share prohibited even traded; Chairman piece unavailable. Invested workshop no bonus/failure VP. Ten-share cap but investments continue without new shares.
grades.observed_answer: After Family share creation and before Hiring, players may take firm investment actions in any order until no one wishes to act; firm managers resolve timing conflicts within a firm and the PM resolves conflicts between firms. A player may form a firm only if they currently manage none: return one eligible Company share to supply or flip a workshop to its invested side, flip the family board, place a family member as the first firm share, set value to the leftmost track space, and take £5 from the bank into the London treasury. To invest in a firm, get its manager’s consent and contribute a Company share or workshop, creating a firm share and placing £5 from the bank in London. A firm can have at most ten shares; further investments still contribute £5 but create no shares. The Chairman share cannot be used; a Company share cannot be invested when Standing and/or Debt is on a lined space; and shares created this turn cannot be invested, even if traded away. Invested workshops never return to uninvested, including after firm failure, and give neither workshop bonus nor Company-failure VP. Family cash cannot be transferred into or out of firm treasuries except through specified procedures.
grades.reason: Nonmanager formation and manager-consented investment, eligible share/workshop contributions and £5 bank-to-London funds, initial share/value, weak/immature/Chairman restrictions and permanent workshop/ten-share effects are supplied.

grades.question: Explain firm trading strategy, when checks and order filling occur, initiative, capacity, repeat-filled revenue and firm value growth.
grades.expected_answer: After investments managers secretly choose home/sea zone and London cash bid; need ship, may choose even closed home. Reveal cash but not strategy. At associated Presidency start reveal/check once with bid dice, pay bank. Success initiative ships minus number of 1/2 dice; President successful Trade gets same calculation. Fill lowest initiative first, President breaks ties; absent/nontrading President wait for Commander/Governors and Chairman breaks ties. Firm fills max ships+1 open connected orders from chosen home once each; prior-fill by others allowed for half listed value rounded down. Revenue India, advance value one space per £6 revenue this turn. Company may also fill orders previously filled by firms this turn at half listed value, rounded down, retaining normal President and writer bonuses.
grades.observed_answer: Each firm gets exactly one trade attempt per turn. Managers simultaneously and secretly choose a trade zone/home port, requiring at least one ship, and commit a secret cash bid from London, or choose Hobnob, which has no bid, trade, or dividends but still pays expenses and retains its previous dividend marker. A closed home port is allowed when choosing the strategy. Reveal bids simultaneously but keep strategy cards facedown until their matching Presidency begins. At the start of that Presidency’s operations, before any actions, reveal matching strategies and roll one die per committed £1, paying the bid to the bank; at least one 1 or 2 permits trade. Firm initiative is ship count minus successful dice (1s/2s), possibly negative. The President’s successful Trade sets its initiative the same way. After that success, fill orders in ascending initiative; the President chooses ties, so the Company does not automatically go first. If the President is vacant or does not successfully trade, firms fill after the Commander and Governors have had their opportunity, with the Chairman choosing initiative ties. A firm fills as many open orders as possible up to ships plus one, beginning at its selected home port and tracing a connected route back there; it can fill any particular order only once. Place filled tokens and pay revenue to the firm’s India treasury. Firms may refill orders filled by others this turn, and the Company may refill firm orders; a previously filled order pays half its listed revenue, rounded down. Advance firm Value one space for every full £6 added to its India treasury that turn.
summary_evidence: Deregulation — Firm strategies and competing trade
grades.source_references: Rules p40; lines 2773–2822; Rules p40 lines2817–2820; p41 example
grades.reason: Secret strategy and public-bid/private-card timing, closed-home and single-attempt constraints, check/payment and initiative, both tie authorities/timing, ships-plus-one route and one fill per order, reciprocal half-revenue refills and £6 India-based value growth are resolved.

grades.question: How are firm expenses and dividends funded and calculated, and what happens to a failing firm, its shares and workshops?
grades.expected_answer: Start Revenue firms act initiative order then others, ties manager windows then PM clockwise. Expenses £1 per ship plus max(shares, firm value); either treasury. If cannot pay dissolution (or emergency rescue): shares Debtors Prison -1 VP each, ships shipyards, charter family, invested workshops stay invested. Dividends only India, £1 per share plus £1 manager each; shareholder may forgo with manager consent. Record total paid retirement marker then sweep remainder India to London.
grades.observed_answer: At the start of Revenue, firms pay expenses before the Company, in initiative order, then other firms; ties go to the manager with most windows, then PM clockwise order. Pay £1 per charter ship plus the higher of the firm’s share count or firm value, using either or both firm treasuries. After expenses, the manager may pay dividends only from the India treasury. Each dividend pays £1 per firm share plus £1 to the manager; with the manager’s consent, a shareholder may forgo payment for any number of shares on any dividend. Record total actual cash paid, not the per-share amount, as the dividend marker. An active firm other than a Hobnob firm that pays none records zero; Hobnob retains its prior marker. Sweep remaining India money into London. If the firm cannot pay expenses, it dissolves unless rescued. On dissolution, shares go to Debtor’s Prison (−1 VP each), ships return to shipyards, the charter returns to the family side, and workshops remain invested. Rescue options are emergency investments under normal Company-share/workshop rules—even if the ten-share cap prevents more shares—which pay expenses, lose any remaining cash, and lower Value one space per emergency investment; or merge with one other firm, which must first pay its own expenses if not already paid and cover the endangered firm’s unpaid expenses.
summary_evidence: Deregulation — Firm expenses, rescue and dividends

grades.question: During attrition, how does an office roll resolve, what extra modifier does the Chairman have, and where do a retiring member, card and fatigue go?

grades.observed_answer: During London Season attrition, simultaneously roll one die for each held office card. Add one for each fatigue on that card, and add one more for the Chairman. A modified 1–2 has no effect; 3–4 adds fatigue to the card; 5+ retires the officeholder. Move a retiring member to Pensioners, flip the office card into Vacant Offices, and return its fatigue to supply. Commanders have no office card and do not make this normal attrition roll.

grades.question: Who may select London Season cards, in what order and with which tiebreakers? What happens to the display and unused pensioners afterward?

grades.observed_answer: Only players who retired at least one pensioner may select or discard one card from the London Season display. Do not replace cards while players are selecting; if the display empties, immediately skip all remaining eligible players. After selections, discard every card left in the display and refill it with exactly three cards: prestige faceup and blackmail facedown, even if nobody took a card. Return all unused Pensioners to their supplies; they do not carry over.
grades.reason: Eligibility, actual spending order, both tiebreakers, take/discard, no immediate replacement, empty-display skip, faceup/down refill and pensioner return are resolved.

grades.question: How do the opportunity marker and extra-action laws affect family actions? If four offices are vacant and the marker already sits on Enlist Writer, how many writers can be placed?

grades.observed_answer: At the start of the Family phase, each player checks where their opportunity marker was at phase start. They choose a main family action once, or may take it twice if the marker already matched that action; then they move the marker onto the chosen main action. Afterward, only the latest passed extra-action law may grant an extra action. That law's action is never doubled by the opportunity marker and does not move the marker. With at least four vacant offices, Enlist Writer places one additional writer once this turn, so a doubled Enlist Writer action places three writers total. grades.reason: Ordinary main action, phase-start matching/doubling, marker movement, latest extra law without marker effects and three-writer once-per-turn bonus are resolved.

grades.question: After Seek Share actions, how are new Company shares created and remaining applicants moved? Where was the initial purchase money paid?

Pieces in Court are Company shares. If Debt reaches zero while applicants remain, slide them as far right as possible while preserving their order. When a player seeks a share, they place a family member on an empty Stock Exchange space and pay the bank the printed queue cost (£2, £3, £3, £4, or £5); that piece is only an applicant at that point, not yet a share. summary_evidence: II. Family — Seek Share; New Company shares

grades.question: When hiring, how are vacancies ordered, what consent does hiring your own family require, what happens to promoted fatigue, and what if no candidate or hirer exists?

grades.question: How is a Chairman elected, how does a deadlocked election resolve, and does the elected Chairman piece remain a tradable Company share?

grades.observed_answer: The former Chairman first announces how many shares are needed for a pure majority, meaning more than half of current shares. Any shareholder may campaign; the first candidate supported by players controlling that many shares wins. Move one of the winner's Company shares into the Chairman slot and give them the title marker. That Chairman piece still counts as a share for dividends, majority calculations, and scoring, but cannot be traded or invested in a firm. If nobody wins by majority support, the former Chairman chooses any shareholder, including themself, without Nepotism consent. grades.question: Explain success-check results, payment, retries, catastrophic destinations and the restriction against dead actions.
grades.expected_answer: Commit office treasury money/resources, gather dice then subtract penalty; lowest die 1–2 success, 3–4 failure retry if sufficient resources, 5–6 catastrophe: no more office actions, officeholder to supply, card flipped to Vacant Offices, fatigue to supply (specific office exceptions apply). No action without effect or chance of success.

Gather dice, subtract penalties, and roll. Use the lowest die: 1–2 succeeds; 3–4 fails and can be retried if resources and office-specific limits allow; 5–6 is catastrophic failure, ends that office's actions, returns its officeholder to supply, discards fatigue, and flips its card into Vacant Offices. Specific Commander and firm procedures can modify these rules. Do not take a dead action with no effect or chance of success, such as trying to trade without a ship or deploying without dice merely to trigger possible officer losses.
grades.reason: Acting-office cash paid to bank, resources minus penalty, lowest-die results/retries, catastrophic destinations and no-dead-action rule are explicit.

grades.question: What are the Chairman’s voluntary borrowing and allocation duties, including consent and track limits?
grades.expected_answer: May advance Debt three times freely, +£5 Balance each. Each further advancement needs majority-shareholder consent including Chairman share; cannot pass Debt track end. Must allocate all Company Balance to other office treasuries, reducing Balance accordingly; borrowing may interleave allocation while respecting limit.
grades.observed_answer: The Chairman may freely add up to three Debt, receiving £5 Balance for each advance, and never advance beyond the Debt track end. Each additional advance beyond those three requires consent from players controlling a majority of Company shares, counting the Chairman. The Chairman must then allocate all Balance to other offices' treasuries, reducing Balance by each transfer. Borrowing and allocation may be interleaved, provided the total borrowing follows the same limits. Cash already in office treasuries remains there for those offices to use.
grades.reason: Three free £5 advances, further majority consent including Chairman, track limit, all-Balance allocation and allowed interleaving are resolved.

grades.question: What must Shipping do with its budget? State ship costs, destinations, consent requirements and the prerequisite for buying Company ships.

The manager may lease an extra ship for £2, fit a ship from a shipyard for £3 without the shipyard owner's consent, or buy a Company ship for £5 only if no ships remain on shipyards. Each acquired ship may be placed in any sea zone, including China once that office exists. Extra ships last only until Refresh. A firm has separate purchase rules: it pays £3 from its London treasury to fit a ship from a shipyard with the owner's consent; it may buy a player-owned ship already in the Company with that owner's consent for £3 if unfatigued or £2 if fatigued, paying the price into Shipping's treasury. summary_evidence: Actions — Manager of Shipping; Firms phase: investments — Ships
grades.reason: Mandatory spending endpoint, all three costs, shipyard consent waiver, Company-ship prerequisite and sea-zone destinations are supplied.

grades.question: For a President’s Trade action, explain declared regions, dice penalty, routes and capacity, insufficient writers, protected home regions, bonuses and successful-trade limit.

Success fill as many orders as possible in declared regions, one per ship, first home port then adjacent own placed writers. Use filled tokens if writers exhausted. Cannot fill another Presidency home region even vacant. Company receives printed order values, President £1 per filled order, writer owner £1 per writer placed; at most one successful trade per President per turn. Revenue exception: under Deregulation an order already filled by a firm this turn pays the Company half listed value, rounded down; President and writer bonuses remain unchanged.

The President spends £1 from that Presidency's treasury per die and subtracts one die per declared nonhome region. A failure can be retried during the President's uninterrupted opportunity if affordable; another position cannot act between that President's attempts. Catastrophe removes the President. A President may have at most one successful Trade per turn. On success, fill one order per ship in its sea zone, as many as possible within declared regions: the first writer goes to the home port, and each next order must be adjacent to one already filled by this Presidency. Use actual writers while available, then filled-order tokens. A President cannot fill another Presidency's home region even if that other office is vacant. Increase Company Balance by each order's printed value, or half rounded down if a firm already filled that order this turn under deregulation. The President receives £1 from the bank per order, and owners receive £1 per writer they placed. Place dividers between adjacent writers from different Presidencies for their return at Refresh.
grades.source_references: Rules pp20–21; lines 1540–1582; Rules p40 lines2817–2820; p41 example

grades.question: What can a Commander target with Deploy, what produces dice and penalties, and when and how are officer losses checked?
grades.expected_answer: Target home, associated region or bordering associated region; exclude another home or another Presidency Company region. Own Company target requires closed order/unrest. Exhaust active officers/regiments for one die each, alliances for printed strength, subtract the combined strength of target and all OTHER regions in its empire (target counted once); Company-controlled defending strength zero. After every attempt roll per exhausted officer, each 6 removes an officer to its owner supply, never regiment.
grades.observed_answer: A Commander may target their own Presidency's home region, any region associated with that Presidency, or a region bordering one of its associated regions. They may not target another Presidency's home region or another Presidency's Company-controlled region; a Company region must have unrest or a closed order for the action to have an effect. For each attempt, exhaust officers and regiments for one die apiece and local alliances for their printed number of dice. Subtract the combined strength of the target and all other regions in its empire, counting the target only once; Company-controlled defense strength is zero. Roll the normal check; a noncatastrophic failure may be retried with remaining resources. After every attempt, owners roll one die for each officer exhausted in that attempt; each 6 returns that officer to supply. Regiments do not roll for losses.

grades.question: On successful Deploy how are loot and trophies calculated and control imposed? What changes if Deploy catastrophically fails?
grades.expected_answer: Loot £4 per tower plus faceup loot modifier, at least surviving used officers+1. Pay Commander £1 plus £1 per own used surviving officer, clockwise other officers, then £1 bank per regiment/alliance piece; repeat until empty. Commander trophy per tower; remove tower/dome, capital matching flags, clear unrest/open all orders. Newly conquer: loot token region-side above President, Governor overlay placed in conquered region and ONLY office card to Vacant Offices stack, Company control; inward redirect Elephant if formerly poised outward there. Catastrophe loses half trophies rounded up and Commander to supply; still check exhausted officer losses.
grades.observed_answer: On a successful Deploy, take loot from the bank equal to £4 per target tower plus the faceup loot modifier, with a minimum equal to the number of participating officers who survive this attempt plus £1. Distribute repeatedly in cycles, stopping when loot runs out: first the Commander receives £1 plus £1 for each of their used surviving officers; then, clockwise, other families receive £1 per used surviving officer they have; last the bank receives £1 per used regiment and per used local-alliance piece regardless of its strength. Repeat the whole cycle from the Commander until all loot is distributed. The Commander also gains one trophy per target tower. Then remove the target's tower and dome; if it was an empire capital, remove all matching empire flags. Open all its orders and remove all its unrest. If it was not Company-controlled, form a Governorship: put the loot/control token region-side up above its President's box, place the Governor overlay on the conquered region, and send only the office card to Vacant Offices for later hiring; do not create Governors/overlays if Governor General is in play. If the Elephant faced outward from the conquered region, move it fully inside. On catastrophic failure, the Commander returns half their family's trophies rounded up and the Commander member returns to supply; exhausted officers still check for losses. The Commander has no office card to vacate.
grades.reason: Loot formula/minimum, clockwise repeating payout and bank pieces, trophies, capital/Elephant cleanup, new Governorship destinations and catastrophic trophy/member/loss effects are resolved.

grades.question: How does Governor Administer work across repeated attempts, including bonuses, tax unrest and stopping?
grades.expected_answer: Start printed dice pool; roll pool, no penalty, lose one die after any attempt. Success £1 bonus, extra £1 if preceding roll failed, choose build Company ship in two successful stages, regiment in associated army, or unsplit £2 Balance/President treasury. Tax after first in turn adds unrest. Any unsuccessful check adds unrest. May repeat until stop, pool exhausted or catastrophe (general vacancy rule).
grades.observed_answer: A Governor uses the printed dice pool for an attempt without a penalty, then reduces the pool by one after every attempt regardless of its result. On success, take £1, or £2 if the immediately preceding roll was unsuccessful, then choose exactly one benefit: build a Company ship (after two successful Build actions, place a partially built ship in the region if none is there, otherwise complete it into the sea zone associated with that Governor's President); commission a regiment into that President's Army; or Tax by adding an unsplit £2 to Company Balance or that President's treasury. Each Tax after the first this turn adds unrest in the region. Any unsuccessful roll adds one unrest there; catastrophe also removes the officeholder under the normal rule. Repeat with the shrinking pool until the Governor chooses to stop, has no dice remaining, or catastrophically fails.
grades.reason: Independent fresh borderline adjudication: wording makes two successful Builds a prerequisite to placing a partial ship, leaving first-stage timing unresolved. Other requested mechanics/destinations correct.

grades.question: If Company revenue cannot cover expenses, how do emergency loans work at and below max Debt, how does Standing change, and when are expectations and dividends checked?
grades.expected_answer: Expenses £1 per current Debt, officer/regiment excluding Commander, ship in sea zones including China. Emergency loans +£5 each, advance Debt if possible even at maximum continue borrowing; added Debt costs no current-turn interest, then Balance zero. 1–2 emergency loans Standing -1; 3+ -2. Then compare Balance with expectations at current Standing, if below Standing -1. Then optional dividends £1 per share incl Chairman; total dividend payout strictly greater than expectations advances Standing once. Immediate failure when Standing reaches failure.
grades.observed_answer: At Revenue, Company expenses reduce Balance by £1 for each existing Debt, each officer or regiment in an Army, and each ship in a sea zone, including China; Commanders are excluded. If Balance cannot cover expenses, take £5 emergency loans, advancing Debt one each until its track end, and continue taking emergency loans even at maximum Debt. Newly added emergency Debt creates no additional expense this turn. After the loans, set Balance to zero. One or two loans lower Standing one space; three or more lower it two. Then compare remaining Balance with expectations at current Standing; if it is below expectations, lower Standing one. Finally the Chairman may pay any affordable number of dividends, costing £1 per Company share each and paying each owner £1 per share, including the Chairman. If total cash paid as dividends is strictly greater than expectations, advance Standing one space.
grades.reason: Loan amount/track-cap/no-current-turn-interest, zero Balance, Standing loan bands, current expectations next, optional dividends and strict enthusiasm inequality are supplied; unasked expense/dividend formulas are not required.

grades.question: When Company regions face a Crisis, which regions are attacked, in what order and at what strength? How is defense mounted and what happens on successful defense?
grades.expected_answer: Resolve primary first then all other Company regions with unrest, Bombay/Madras/Bengal Army order; each Commander orders own regions. Primary normal invasion/rebellion strength + local unrest, secondary unrest only. Exhaust newly active Army strength equal attack or as much as possible; insufficient means Region Loss. Successful defense clears unrest and Commander gains trophy. Vacant Commander replaced by Military Affairs then Chairman, acting substitute gains/loses no trophies. Additionally, if the primary Crisis was a normal Invasion which failed against the Company, remove one tower level from the attacker if possible.
grades.observed_answer: When an Invasion or Rebellion attacks a Company region, resolve the primary attack first, then secondary Rebellions in every other Company region that has unrest, in Bombay, Madras, Bengal order; each Presidency's Commander orders attacks within that Presidency. A normal primary Crisis attack strength is the ordinary Invasion/Rebellion strength plus unrest in the target region. A primary Foreign Invasion uses only its ordinary attack die, with no added unrest. Each secondary Rebellion's strength is only the unrest cubes in that secondary region, with no event modifier or empire strength. The associated Commander must exhaust active Army pieces whose strength totals the attack strength, or as much as possible; local alliances count at printed strength and cannot be split. If newly exhausted defense strength is insufficient, resolve Region Loss. If sufficient, remove all unrest in that attacked region and give the Commander one trophy. If this successful defense defeated a normal primary Invasion, also remove one tower from the attacking region if possible. If the Commander is vacant, Military Affairs acts in their stead, or the Chairman if Military Affairs is vacant; that player chooses defense pieces and gains or loses no trophies, and no new Commander is appointed.
summary_evidence: VII. Events in India — Attacks on Company; Region Loss
grades.source_references: Rules p33; lines 2262–2296; Rules p33 lines2290–2296
grades.reason: Historical frozen key: primary-first and Presidency/Commander order, unrest-only secondaries, primary strength, compulsory defense and vacant substitutes, trophy/unrest cleanup and failed-primary-Invasion attacker tower loss are supplied. Subsequent source-gap discovery invalidates any complete core signoff for excess alliance strength.
grades.source_completeness_warning: Historical key did not settle an indivisible alliance exceeding attack strength. Correct means recovery of the historical asked/known procedure only; no definitive overshoot ruling or complete core PASS.

grades.question: What happens when a law fails versus passes, including support-zero, policy movement, Prime Minister and effect order?
grades.expected_answer: Support -1 or lower fails; discard and resolve dilemma If Failed, Opposition Leader returns marker and becomes PM, moves selected policy one adjacent space either way and resolves it. Zero or higher passes: law with passed laws, PM gains token, selected policy consequence then immediate law effects. Restore vote cards. If legislation fails Company, finish vote then final scoring.
grades.observed_answer: The PM reveals up to three laws one at a time, chooses one, discards the others, chooses the direction around the policy dial, and stops at the first policy space matching the law's bottom icon. Set Vote to the law's printed starting support. Players vote starting with the PM and clockwise; each £1 of family cash buys one vote, plus printed card votes. Support can move up or down, and tracks are unlimited. The PM may call another full round or stop after each; a round with no votes must end voting. A player who voted for may later oppose, but after opposing cannot vote for during that vote. Track opposition votes; the largest opponent holds Opposition Leader, with the current holder keeping it on a tie. With the recipient's consent, votes may be cast for someone who already opposed or commits to oppose, and are added to that person's opposition total. The PM cannot oppose or consent to enterprises opposing except when forced by the specified promise. At support −1 or less, the law fails: discard it, resolve a dilemma's If Failed text, return Opposition Leader's token, and give that player the PM dial; the new PM moves the proposed policy one space in either direction and resolves that adjacent policy. At support zero or more, the law passes: place it with passed laws, give the PM a passed-law token, resolve the selected policy first, then the law's immediate effects. In either outcome, restore used voting cards to their regular orientation. If the law causes Company failure, finish the vote before Final Scoring.
grades.reason: Negative failure versus zero-or-positive passage, law/dilemma handling, PM transfer/adjacent policy, policy-before-immediate-law order, vote-card restoration and finish-vote failure timing are supplied.

grades.question: When can or must a Deregulation session be called in the relevant scenarios, and what are its success/failure effects and exceptions from ordinary voting?
grades.expected_answer: 1758/Long1710 start-turn before London: PM may if Standing and/or Debt lined, must if either starred. Pass reduce Debt one per two Debt, Standing to S, PM law token, activate deregulation. Failure raise share VP value up to ±3, law kept, PM stays. No policy and PM may vote against.
grades.observed_answer: In the 1758 and Long 1710 scenarios, at the start of a turn before London Season, the PM may call a special Deregulation vote if Standing and/or Debt is on a lined space, and must call it if either is on a starred space. Use the ordinary voting procedure and support threshold. If it passes, lower Debt by one for every two current Debt, set Standing to S, give the PM a passed-law token, and activate firms. If it fails, increase Company share scoring value by flipping or placing the Court VP token, up to a maximum of ±3. This special vote has no policy; failure neither removes the PM nor discards the Deregulation law, and the PM may vote against it. The 1813 scenario starts deregulated.
grades.reason: Correct scenarios/before-London timing, lined/starred triggers, both outcomes, share-value cap and all special voting exceptions are resolved.

grades.question: How can a firm be formed or invested in, where does money come from, and what restrictions apply to Company shares, invested workshops and the ten-share limit?
grades.expected_answer: Nonmanager forms by returning eligible Company share or flipping workshop invested; flip own board, create family firm share, value leftmost, £5 bank to London. Later investment manager consent, same share/workshop payment gives £5 London and new share. Weak Company share when Standing/Debt lined prohibited; same-turn share prohibited even traded; Chairman piece unavailable. Invested workshop no bonus/failure VP. Ten-share cap but investments continue without new shares.
grades.observed_answer: After Family share creation and before Hiring, investment actions occur without a set order until nobody wants more; the firm manager resolves timing conflicts within a firm and the PM resolves conflicts between firms. To form a firm, a player must currently manage none; return one eligible Company share to supply or flip a workshop to its invested side, flip the family board, place a family member as the first firm share, set Value to its leftmost space, and take £5 from the bank into the London treasury. To invest in an existing firm, get the manager's consent and contribute an eligible Company share or flip a workshop to its invested side; this creates one firm share and puts £5 from the bank into London. A firm can have at most ten shares; further investments still contribute £5 but create no share. The Chairman share cannot be contributed. No Company shares may be invested while Standing and/or Debt is on a lined space, and a Company share created this turn cannot be invested, even if traded away. Family cash cannot be transferred into or out of firm treasuries. An invested workshop never returns to uninvested status, gives no workshop bonus or Company-failure VP, and stays invested if the firm fails.
grades.reason: Nonmanager formation and manager-consented investment, eligible share/workshop contributions and £5 bank-to-London funds, initial share/value, weak/immature/Chairman restrictions and permanent workshop/ten-share effects are supplied.

grades.question: Explain firm trading strategy, when checks and order filling occur, initiative, capacity, repeat-filled revenue and firm value growth.
grades.expected_answer: After investments managers secretly choose home/sea zone and London cash bid; need ship, may choose even closed home. Reveal cash but not strategy. At associated Presidency start reveal/check once with bid dice, pay bank. Success initiative ships minus number of 1/2 dice; President successful Trade gets same calculation. Fill lowest initiative first, President breaks ties; absent/nontrading President wait for Commander/Governors and Chairman breaks ties. Firm fills max ships+1 open connected orders from chosen home once each; prior-fill by others allowed for half listed value rounded down. Revenue India, advance value one space per £6 revenue this turn. Company may also fill orders previously filled by firms this turn at half listed value, rounded down, retaining normal President and writer bonuses.
grades.observed_answer: Each firm has exactly one trade attempt per turn. Managers simultaneously and secretly choose either a trade zone/home port (the firm must have at least one ship, may choose even if its home port is closed, and commits a secret cash bid from London) or Hobnob (no bid, trade, or dividends; expenses still apply and the old dividend marker remains for retirement). Bids are revealed together, while strategy cards stay facedown until the matching Presidency begins. At that Presidency's operations start, before actions, matching firms reveal strategies, roll one die per committed £1, and pay the bid to the bank. At least one 1 or 2 permits the trade; initiative equals ship count minus the number of successful dice, so it may be negative. A President's successful Trade generates initiative the same way from Presidency ships. After that success, fill orders from lowest initiative upward; the President chooses the order among ties, so the Company is not automatically first. If the President is vacant or never trades successfully, firms fill after Commander/Governors had their chance, with the Chairman choosing initiative ties. A firm fills open orders up to ships plus one, starting at its chosen home port and tracing its own filled route back to that port; it cannot fill any particular order more than once. Firms may refill orders filled earlier that turn by others or the Company, and the Company may refill firm-filled orders. Put trade revenue in the firm's India treasury. An order already filled that turn yields half its listed revenue, rounded down. Advance firm Value one space for each full £6 added to India treasury that turn.
grades.source_references: Rules p40; lines 2773–2822; Rules p40 lines2817–2820; p41 example
grades.reason: Secret strategy and public-bid/private-card timing, closed-home and single-attempt constraints, check/payment and initiative, both tie authorities/timing, ships-plus-one route and one fill per order, reciprocal half-revenue refills and £6 India-based value growth are resolved.

grades.question: How are firm expenses and dividends funded and calculated, and what happens to a failing firm, its shares and workshops?
grades.expected_answer: Start Revenue firms act initiative order then others, ties manager windows then PM clockwise. Expenses £1 per ship plus max(shares, firm value); either treasury. If cannot pay dissolution (or emergency rescue): shares Debtors Prison -1 VP each, ships shipyards, charter family, invested workshops stay invested. Dividends only India, £1 per share plus £1 manager each; shareholder may forgo with manager consent. Record total paid retirement marker then sweep remainder India to London.
grades.observed_answer: At the start of Revenue, before the Company, firms pay expenses in initiative order and then other firms; ties go by the manager with most windows, then PM-clockwise order. Expenses are £1 per charter ship plus the higher of the firm's share count or Value, payable from either or both firm treasuries. If the firm cannot pay, it dissolves unless rescued. On dissolution, shares go to Debtor's Prison (−1 VP each), ships return to shipyards, and the charter flips back to the family side; invested workshops remain invested. Rescue may use emergency investments under the normal Company-share/workshop rules, even if the ten-share cap prevents creating more shares: pay expenses, lose any remaining cash, and lower Value one space per emergency investment.
